newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank sees debt payoff for provinces.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank sees debt payoff for provinces.

text.p: Shrinking debts and deficits will allow many of Canada's provinces to reduce taxes and increase spending early in the next century, the Royal Bank said in a report released on Tuesday.

"With the exception of Quebec and Ontario, the happy picture of melting debt requires no fiscal pain beyond what has already been prescribed," said Royal Bank chief economist John McCallum, in a statement.
Canada's largest bank said Saskatchewan and the four Atlantic provinces will benefit the most from improving debt situations.
The bank said the five provinces had undergone substantial fiscal restraint and should therefore see the greatest benefits of any of the provinces.
"Under present policies, these provinces could enjoy fiscal dividends on the order of 3.5-4.0 percent of gross domestic product over the next 10 to 20 years," the bank said.

Royal Bank said that could translate into about a two-thirds cut in provincial income tax or a 50 percent hike in provincial health care spending. The provinces could also gradually cut taxes or increase spending over a longer period in step with declining debt ratios, the bank said.

The bank said the prognosis was mixed for the remaining provinces. Quebec and Ontario would have to undergo substantial additional fiscal restraint if they were to achieve their balanced budget targets for the turn of the century, the bank said. Afterward, Quebec and Ontario residents stood to benefit, but not as soon as residents of other provinces, the report said.
Royal Bank said projected fiscal dividends for residents of the three other Western provinces would be significant, but much smaller than for residents of Saskatchewan and Atlantic Canada.
The bank said declining debt and interest payments at the federal level would also translate into major fiscal dividends down the road, providing that the federal government stayed on course.
